note: Adapted from Kemner's 1932 original description (in German). Type locality Depok, western Java, collected on 10 October 1920 (month 10) from an old fallen tree branch. The soldier occurs in distinct large and small forms without essential morphological differences, and the original gives the measurements of both side by side. The original lists the peculiar sclerotization of the 10th abdominal tergite as the most distinctive feature of the species.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head short and thick, in lateral view almost oval because of the projecting postmental region, the frons only slightly inclined, both frontal lobes completely rounded and blunt; antennae 9 (10)-segmented, the middle segments strongly transverse; left mandible with 2 strong triangular teeth at the tip and a 3rd tooth further basally, separated from the first two by a rounded notch; right mandible with 2 very blunt and indistinct teeth. The 10th abdominal tergite is more strongly sclerotized than the others, forming a brownish yellow to brownish black sclerotic plate, a feature the original calls unique among the known Oriental species. The species is distinguished from the previously known East Indian species of Glyptotermes by the very short soldier head.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Brownish black, venter slightly paler; the midline of the first 5 sternites pale; mouthparts, tibiae and tarsi yellow white to yellowish brown. Wings yellowish brown, the costal veins darker. Pilosity sparse. Head large, oval, longer than wide; cephalic sutures indistinct. Compound eyes rather small, distinctly oval; ocelli very small, close against the compound eyes. Labrum rounded-square, about as long as wide, the anterior margin truncate. Antennae short, 11—12-segmented, thickening outwards; with 11 segments the 2nd shorter than the 3rd, with 12 segments the 2nd longer than the 3rd. Pronotum narrower than the head, longer than half its width. Wing membrane finely tuberculate; radius short, reaching only one fifth of the way along the forewing; radial sector and media usually unbranched, occasionally with a short radial sector branch and the media curving down towards the cubitus, in which case the media loses its dark colour immediately after leaving the radial sector. Measurements (mm): body length with wings 5.30—5.80, body length without wings 3.85—4.42, forewing length 4.62, head width 0.74—0.78, pronotal width 0.66—0.70, pronotal length 0.42.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: There are larger and smaller individuals, without essential differences. Head yellowish brown, the front only slightly tinged with brown; mandibles dark only at the tip. Pilosity short and inconspicuous; head and pronotum with a few setae, the abdomen more densely hairy. Head short and thick, in lateral view almost oval because of the projecting postmental region; frons only slightly inclined, both frontal lobes completely rounded and blunt. Labrum rounded-square, about as long as wide. Mandibles short and strong; left mandible with 2 strong triangular teeth at the tip and a 3rd tooth further basally, separated from the first two by a rounded notch; right mandible with 2 very blunt and indistinct teeth. Antennae 9 (10)-segmented, short and stout, the middle segments strongly transverse; 2nd segment longer than the 3rd, the 3rd sometimes extremely short or not yet separated from the 4th, so that a slightly constricted larger 3rd segment appears. Pronotum nearly rectangular, about twice as long as wide (as in the original), the anterior sides parallel, the posterior angles broadly rounded, the anterior margin deeply concave and the posterior margin very shallowly concave. The 10th abdominal tergite is more strongly sclerotized than the others, forming a brownish yellow to brownish black sclerotic plate. Measurements (mm): body length major soldier 5.00, minor soldier 4.00; head length including the mandibles 1.55, 1.52; head length excluding the mandibles 1.27, 1.16; head width 0.88, 0.85; pronotal width 0.85, 0.74.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Nymphs occur with and without wing buds; one mature individual without wing buds measured (mm): body length 5.00, head width 0.8 (printed as "08" in the original), pronotal width 0.77.
